clue.text:
A setter held back by someone flirting?
 A corker, perhaps

indicators.note: held by means kept within the grasp of the flirting word

parts.note: a person who flirts may wink, so is a winker

indicators.note: back means the letters are turned round and read the other way

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as 'me'

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler being detained by a flirt, with an aside about a fine specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corker' looks like slang for something excellent, but here it is literally one who puts the corks in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who produces wine bottles it and stoppers it, so is literally a corker, the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: See 17
Foul word of prayer masked by babble

indicators.note: masked by means hidden inside the other word

parts.note: babble is meaningless noise
om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist prayer

explanation.surface: A dirty prayer drowned out by chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' is the definition: the answer means offensive, not loud, despite its look.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells, not loud.

clue.text: See 17
Silk, rather oddly, used for old gowns

indicators.note: used means worked over, so the letters are rearranged
oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: Silk, a little strangely, was employed for antique dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes RTE from 'rather'; 'used' rearranges SILK plus RTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A kirtle is a woman's long gown or tunic of medieval times, now archaic.

clue.text: Grass around fielder picked up

indicators.note: around means the grass word goes round the fielder

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
cover is a cricket fielding position on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder picks up the ball from the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover is a fielding position on the off side; 'picked up' means improved, not gathered the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Picked up in the sense of got better, as an economy or patient improves.

clue.text: Day-old wrinkly, age-old character

indicators.note: wrinkly suggests something creased and crumpled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something a day old already wrinkled, like an ancient character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrinkly' rearranges DAY plus O into the Star Wars Jedi master.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Wars Jedi master is famously some nine hundred years old, a truly ancient character.

clue.text: See 23
See 22
Pray with private for new recruit

parts.note: to pray someone is to beg or plead
private thoughts are inner ones, kept inside

explanation.surface: An army newcomer prays alongside a private soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' suggests a soldier, which suits 'recruit', but here it is the adjective meaning inner.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh recruit is a novice just starting out in a role.

clue.text: Muncher of grass munching everything green

indicators.note: munching means the animal has the other word in its mouth, inside it

parts.note: a grazing animal like a cow munches grass
everything means all

explanation.surface: A grazing animal chomps through all the green vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the grass colour but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of naive or inexperienced, as a raw youth is.

clue.text: Day piercing scream almost turned sour

indicators.note: piercing means the day goes through the middle of the other letters
turned means the shortened word is read backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to scream is to yell
MON is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: A day when a shriek nearly went sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' acts on the shortened scream only, giving LEY, before the day goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus-flavoured with the sharpness of that fruit, so tart or acidic in taste.

clue.text:
Private chamber I reserved to host first
 of ladies in extravagant fashion

parts.note: a lav, short for lavatory, is a private little room

indicators.note: to host means to take something inside as a guest

parts.note: a reserved person is shy

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A private room, reserved and hosting ladies first, done up extravagantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Lav, short for lavatory, is British slang for a toilet, hence a private chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lavishly means doing it generously and without restraint, an adverb matching the phrase.

clue.text:
Cunning plan — stain at the front is to be
 removed from shirt

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of the word stain
to be removed from means the letters of is are taken out of the garment

parts.note: a chemise is a loose shirt-like garment

explanation.surface: A clever plan to get a stain off the front of a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunning plan' echoes Baldrick in the British comedy Blackadder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning plan is a plot or devious design, a crafty arrangement.

clue.text: Motor race that's cultivated

parts.note: a motor is a car
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A motor race that is refined and sophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests a contest of motors but means a people, a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnation is a garden flower grown by gardeners, so something cultivated.

clue.text:
Imagine this crossword starts out as
 cryptic

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
starts picks the opening letters of each word

explanation.surface: Picture this puzzle beginning as a hard cryptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' gives T and C; 'out' rearranges them with IMAGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means puzzling or mysterious, hard to fathom.

clue.text:
Catch outstanding European leader's
 ultimate revolutionary song

indicators.note: outstanding read as standing outside, so the first word goes round the rest

parts.note: to catch someone's meaning is to see it

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

indicators.note: ultimate picks the final letter

explanation.surface: Grab the last song from a top European leader, a revolutionary one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns DANE plus R into RENAD; 'outstanding' means SEE stands outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song, traditionally sung beneath a window at night.

clue.text:
One promising to keep mum permanently
 in gin, drunk by the sound of it?

definitions.text: One promising to keep mum permanently

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is said aloud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone vowing permanent silence, while in gin and seemingly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the spirit, fitting 'drunk', but it is a trap. PISSED is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks take a vow of silence, so each one promises to keep quiet for life.

clue.text:
To demonstrate
 one's sincerity, eat bread?

definitions.meaning: to back up claims with deeds, especially cash, proving you mean it
bread is slang for cash, and eating means putting it into the face's opening

annotation.spelling: PUT ONE'S MONEY WHERE ONE'S MOUTH IS

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is old slang for cash, so eating bread literally places the cash in your gob.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means backing your words with action or cash to show you are sincere.

clue.text: Paddy beat Republican shortly

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, dropping the final letter

parts.note: Donald Trump, the Republican president

explanation.surface: An Irishman hammered a Republican, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irish name but is British slang for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British informal for a temper fit, a childish outburst of rage.

clue.text: Hill bearing small fruit

indicators.note: bearing means carrying something within, holding it inside

parts.note: Damon Hill is the British Formula One world champion
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A hillside carrying little fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill' is not a slope but the surname of racing driver Damon Hill; 'bearing' puts S inside DAMON.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dark purple plum, often used for jam or gin.

clue.text: See 17
Soldier in art museum, name Frank

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the gallery's letters

parts.note: MoMA is the Museum of Modern Art in New York
a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier in a gallery called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests a man, but it is the soldier ant. 'Frank' looks like a name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-to-man talk is honest and direct, so frank.

clue.text:
Partner joining principal in company with a
 generous corporation

indicators.note: principal means the leading letter of the word company

parts.note: hubby is informal for husband, a partner

explanation.surface: A spouse joins the boss of a firm alongside a big-hearted business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks commercial, suiting 'company', but is old jocular slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is humorous dated slang for a paunch, so having a generous one means being plump.

clue.text:
Dawn's sound party at
 which to sketch spaniels, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals that the phrase is spoken aloud and spelt as heard

parts.words:
party at
 which to sketch spaniels
parts.note: a do is a party, to doodle is to sketch, and cocker spaniels are the dogs, giving a cocker doodle do

explanation.surface: An event at dawn where guests sketch dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: COCKER DOODLE DO, a party for drawing cocker spaniels, said aloud matches the rooster's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooster's crow at daybreak is rendered in English as this call.

clue.text:
I, Russian leader, ostensibly
 tipsy?

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady from drink, so the letters stagger into a new order
leader picks the opening letter of Russian

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler admits he only appears to be tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' rearranges I, R and OSTENSIBLY. The whole clue also describes the man, famous for seeming drunk in public.
explanation.definitionFit: The first president of the Russian Federation was notorious for apparently drunken public appearances.

clue.text: Ruminant occupying hollow tree

indicators.note: occupying means living inside, so the animal sits within the hollow

parts.note: a pit is a hollow in the ground
a gnu or wildebeest chews the cud

explanation.surface: A cud-chewing animal living inside a hollow tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The pignut hickory is a North American tree, so named for its nuts fed to pigs.

clue.text:
Redhead after drunken hack in bar, utterly
 unyielding

indicators.note: in places the assembled letters inside the bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar

indicators.note: after puts the red letter behind the rearranged letters
drunken suggests staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired man follows a drunken journalist in a pub, utterly stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' makes CKHA from the hack. 'Bar' suggests a pub but is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as firm as stone yields not at all, hence utterly unyielding.

clue.text: See 17
Sharp instrument happens to nip hand

indicators.note: to nip means to pinch something, holding it within

parts.note: comes as in comes about, happens
to hand something over is to pass it

explanation.surface: A sharp tool that happens to pinch your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happens' is a verb giving a verb, as in what comes about; 'hand' is likewise the verb, to pass over.
explanation.definitionFit: The drawing tool for circles has a sharp point fixed into the paper.
